newsitem.title: USA: FULL TEXT-Dayton Hudson sets $134 mln charge.
newsitem.headline: FULL TEXT-Dayton Hudson sets $134 mln charge.

text.p: Dayton Hudson Corp said it will take a pretax charge against fourth quarter earnings of $134 million, or $0.35 a share, to write down real estate and store closing costs.
The company said it planned to reposition its real estate, including its Mervyn's division leaving the Florida and Georgia markets.
This is the full text of its announcement.

MINNEAPOLIS, Jan. 17 /PRNewswire/ -- Dayton Hudson Corporation (NYSE: DH) today announced it is undertaking a real estate repositioning effort to strengthen its businesses and position them for long-term growth. The real estate strategy includes the following actions:
-- The exit of Mervyn's from the Florida and Georgia markets;
-- The sale or closure of approximately 10 Mervyn's stores in
-- The renovation of Marshall Field's downtown Milwaukee store.

Including the effect of the previously announced Marshall Field's dispositions in Texas and the closure of Marshall Field's Park Forest, Ill. store, the real estate actions will result in a one-time pre-tax charge against fourth-quarter fiscal 1996 earnings of $134 million, or 35 cents per share, for the writedown of real estate and store closing costs.

As a result of this series of real estate transactions, Dayton Hudson expects to generate approximately $350 million in cash, which will be used to reduce debt and further enhance the company's growth opportunities.

The net impact of these actions at Mervyn's will be to reduce annual revenue by approximately $375 million, based on 1996 performance. As previously disclosed, the net impact of these actions at the Department Store Division will be a reduction of approximately $130 million in annual revenue. In the future, interest savings are expected to substantially offset the impact of these actions on operating profit at both Mervyn's and the Department Store Division.

"Our three retail divisions are core to Dayton Hudson's overall corporate strategy. We remain committed to our objective of improving the performance of the corporation and believe that this real estate repositioning will help us strengthen our competitive position and achieve our long-term financial goals," said Bob Ulrich, Dayton Hudson chairman and chief executive officer.

Dayton Hudson is negotiating or has entered into a series of agreements to sell Mervyn's 25 stores in Florida and Georgia. Dillard Department Stores Inc. has agreed to purchase 10 of 18 Florida locations; JCPenney has agreed to purchase three of seven Georgia locations. The remaining properties are expected to be sold to a variety of other purchasers. It is expected that many of the 2,100 affected Mervyn's employees in Florida and Georgia will receive job offers from Target Stores. "Given Mervyn's limited market penetration in Florida and Georgia, it became clear that the best course of action was to exit these markets," said Ulrich.

In addition, Dayton Hudson will sell or close approximately 10 poor-performing Mervyn's stores throughout the chain. The stores will be sold or will close in the next 12 to 18 months. The majority of affected employees are expected to be offered positions at other Mervyn's stores in those markets.

At the Department Store Division, the downtown Milwaukee Marshall Field's store is being written down to its estimated fair market value in anticipation of a sale-leaseback transaction related to the renovation of the store.

Dayton Hudson Corporation operates large-store general merchandise formats, including discount stores, moderate-priced promotional and traditional department stores. The company currently operates 1,101 stores in 38 states. This includes 736 Target stores, 300 Mervyn's stores and 65 Department Stores.
